questions.question: Define the coefficient of linear expansivity and write its formula and SI unit.
questions.solution:
**Definition:** The coefficient of linear expansivity $\alpha$ of a solid is defined as the **increase in length per unit original length per unit rise in temperature**.

**Formula:**
$$\alpha = \frac{\Delta L}{L_0 \Delta T} = \frac{L_T - L_0}{L_0 \Delta T}$$
where $\Delta L = L_T - L_0$ is the change in length.

**From the new length:** $L_T = L_0(1 + \alpha\Delta T)$

**SI unit:** $\text{K}^{-1}$ or $^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$ (same, since a temperature interval of 1 K equals 1 degree Celsius). Dimensional formula: $\left[T^{-1}\right]$.

**Values:** Aluminium $\approx 23 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{K}^{-1}$, brass $\approx 19 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{K}^{-1}$, steel $\approx 11 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{K}^{-1}$, glass $\approx 9 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{K}^{-1}$.
questions.knowledgeNote: Linear expansivity is the fractional increase in length per degree rise in temperature, with SI unit per kelvin.
